detail:
Decisions: Chose to answer the subagent store-routing question by reading the server's root-resolution code rather than continuing to query the dispatched subagent — reason: the agent returned two idle notifications and no report across two requests, and resolveProjectRoot in src/index.ts settles the question definitively in one read while an agent's self-report would have been weaker evidence anyway. Rejected alternative: keep pinging the subagent for its account, reason_rejected: low expected value against a non-responding agent, and its answer could not have outranked direct evidence from the code plus both stores' contents.
Findings: ANSWERED — closes the open question in finding 01KZ9KZX1QVQ75YVH9SNEG7QA8 and CONFIRMS the candidate mechanism in 01KZ9KZX2X60QX78VRGT07YKYD. src/index.ts:38-44 resolves the project root ONCE at server startup via resolveProjectRoot(--project arg > TWINING_PROJECT env > process.cwd()). The binding is per-server-process, not per-call and not per-agent, so a subagent sharing the session's MCP server inherits the parent's store no matter what its own working directory is. Cross-repo Twining recording by subagent is structurally impossible, not an operator mistake.; The content-scorer session's misfiling (finding 01KZ77G2PM12N8AN2P6T2W5KP3) is therefore fully explained: that session's server was rooted at twining-mcp, so records naming only twining-benchmark-harness files were written here by construction. No amount of prompt discipline in the agent would have prevented it. Reclassify from operator error to design limit.; There IS a supported escape hatch and it is worth surfacing in docs: TWINING_PROJECT env var or the --project argument (#46) override cwd at startup. A second MCP server instance pointed at another repo would record correctly. This was not usable from within an already-running session.; Empirical confirmation independent of the subagent's own report: a subagent dispatched to record into the harness store wrote nothing to EITHER store — harness newest decision record still dated Aug 3, twining-mcp newest was the parent session's own. It also never returned a report, emitting only idle notifications, so its stop-on-wrong-routing instruction cannot be credited for the clean outcome; treat 'no misfiling occurred' as verified by direct inspection of both stores, not by the agent's compliance.
summary: Closed the open routing question: store binding is per-server-process, fixed at startup, so a subagent structurally cannot record into another repo's store. Confirms the misfiling was a design limit.
